To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the skin of subjects with onchocercal infection, but not of uninfected individuals, expressed eotaxin by the vascular endothelium at 24 h after ivermec- tin administration.
the dermal endothelial cells express eotaxin (CCL11) and RANTES (CCL5) after the ivermectine treatment of onchoccerciasis.
the dermal endothelial cells express eotaxin after the treatment with ivermectine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of the immune response to the filarial nematode Onchocerca.
the mechanisms of eosinophil recruitment in the dermal microvasculature of patients with onchocercal disease.
the development of a vaccine to protect humans from infection by Onchocerca.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
eotaxin is the main chemokine that mediates the eosinophil recruitment in the skin of onchocerca-infected individuals following ivermecitin treatment.
the endothelial expression of RANTEs and eotaxins is associated with eosnophill infiltration into the skin following ivermactin treatment of onchoecrciasis.
the endothelial expression of RANTEs, eotaxine, and MCP-2 are not associated with the eosinophil infiltration in onchocercasis, and therefore, they do not have any role in the eosinophil recruitment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified two chemokines (eotaxin and MCP3) which are expressed by the dermal microvasculature following ivermecin treatment of onhocerciasis.
the expression of chemokines by dermal endothelum is associated with eosnophils infiltration into the skin following ivermecitn treatment of onchcerciasis.
eotaxin plays a role in eosinophils recruitment in the skin after the treatment with ivermectine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial cells express chemokines and that these may be important in the recruitment of eosinophis and other cells during helminth infection.
the dermal endothelial cells are the source of eotaxins, RANTES and MCP-3, the three main eosinophil chemoattractants, in human skin.

the dermal vascular endothelium is capable of expressing chemokines, and that this expression can be upregulated in the context of an inflammatory response, such as the killing of Onchocerca worms by ivermectintreatment.
